correctness.rationale: Removing bits not in the target and then adding target bits gives an isometric embedding into the hypercube, so a geodesic uses each coordinate at most once. Each extreme-coordinate edge class has F_n edges (count valid words of length n−2 after fixing the neighboring bit to zero). One class gives the cover lower bound, and their disjoint union is in edge general position. An independent exact replay on the assigned geodesics.json (lines 1–402), using fresh inline Python rather than the supplied verifier, regenerated 21/34/55 vertices and 38/71/130 edges, checked the 8/13/21 paths for valid distinct vertices, unit steps and BFS shortestness, and reproduced the entire edge union in each graph. A set in edge general position uses at most two edges in each covering path, giving the matching upper bounds 16/26/42. The recorded package checks were inspected separately; neither the proof nor the replay covers n>8.
